title: Story of the Sultan of Al-Yaman and His Three Sons

full_text:
In ancient Yemen reigned a wise Sultan who, on his deathbed, left his vast kingdom to his three sons, commanding:
'Go to the Chief Judge of the Desert, Sage Al-Mustansir, whenever a dispute arises, for his discernment will guide your steps.'

After their father's burial, the three princes rode across the sand dunes toward the judge's oasis. As they traveled, they noticed camel tracks in the sand.

The eldest prince observed: 'The camel that passed here was blind in one eye.'
The second prince remarked: 'It was missing one front tooth.'
The youngest prince added: 'It was lame in its left hind leg, carried a load of sweet honey on one flank, and a load of oil on the other!'

Further along the path, an agitated camel merchant stopped them, shouting: 'Noble youths, have you seen my lost camel?'
The eldest asked: 'Was it blind in one eye?'
'Yes!' cried the merchant.
The second asked: 'Was it missing a tooth?'
'Yes, exactly!'
The youngest asked: 'Was it lame, carrying honey on the right and oil on the left?'
'By heaven, you have seen it! Where is it?'
The princes replied: 'We swear we have never seen your camel with our eyes.'

The merchant, convinced they had stolen his beast and goods, seized their reins and dragged them before Judge Al-Mustansir, accusing them of theft.

The Judge turned to the princes: 'You described the camel with absolute precision. How can you claim innocence?'

The eldest explained: 'My lord, the grass was cropped only on the right side of the path, while lush grass on the left remained untouched. A beast with two eyes feeds equally on both sides; therefore, it was blind in its left eye.'

The second said: 'Where it bit the grass, small tufts were left unbroken in the middle of each bite mark, indicating a missing front tooth.'

The youngest said: 'The prints of three hooves were deep and clear, while the left hind hoof dragged lightly in the sand, proving lameness. Furthermore, swarms of flies clustered on the right side of the trail where honey had dripped, while ants swarmed on the left where oil had fallen!'

The Judge laughed with admiration, dismissed the merchant's charge, and soon after, shepherds found the wandering camel unharmed in a canyon.

Impressed by their extraordinary acumen, Al-Mustansir mediated the succession of the kingdom equitably among the three brothers, who ruled Yemen with balanced judgment and legendary wisdom.
moral: Wisdom and keen observation reveal what hidden secrets conceal, proving that intellect surpasses brute force.
